To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enthalpies of metal-oxygen bond dissociation for metal complexes of &-diketones are in general higher than those of the analogous metal carboxylates, and that the enthalpy of the metal-oxygen bond in the complexes of the metal with a &-diketone depends on the metal, the &-diketonic ligand and the number of &-diketonates bound per metal atom.

the enthalpies of decomposition of metal B-dketonates can be calculated from available thermochemical data, and that the enthalpy of gas-phase dissociation of the metal-oxygen bond in these complexes is strongly influenced by the metal and the nature of the B-dketo group.

the metal-oxygen bond dissociation enthalpy of metal B-dicetonates is strongly dependent on the structure and bonding in these complexes, and the trends in the enthalpies can be explained by the electronic properties of both the metal and the ligand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of metal B-dietonates as ligand complexes.

the development of a theoretical method for the determination of homolytic bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of the metal-oxygen bond in metal β-diketonates, and its application to a large set of compounds, with the goal of establishing the trends in the data as a function of structure, bonding and the nature of the metal ion.
the study of the thermochemical properties of metal complexes of β -diketones, with special emphasis on the metal-oxygen bond strength in these compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
metal-oxygen bond strengths are very sensitive to the metal, and to the nature of the metal-ligand bonding, and to a lesser degree, to the nature of substituents on the β-diketone ligand.
the metal-oxygen bond dissociation enthalpies in these complexes vary from 50-70 kcal mol-1, depending on the metal and the structure of the B-diketone ligands.

the enthalpies of metal-oxygen bond cleavage are very sensitive to the nature of the metal and of the B-diketone ligand, and that the enthalpy of metal-oxygen cleavage in the gas phase is a function of the enthalpy difference between the metal atom and the B-diketonate ligand in the gaseous phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the homolytic metal–oxygen bond-dissaciation enthalpy of the metal–oxygen bonds in metal B-diketone complexes is in the range of 60-100 kcal/mol, and that these values are in general agreement with the values of the homolytic bond-dissociaton enthalpies of the metal–halogen bonds in the corresponding metal halides.

the metal-oxygen bonds are stronger in the complexes of the first transition metals, and the metal-oxygen bond strengths are in the order of the first transition metal complexes > lanthanide complexes > transition metal complexes.

the metal-oxygen bonds of metal B-dketonates are weaker than the metal-oxygen bond in the corresponding oxides, and that the metal-oxygens are more reactive towards nucleophiles than are the oxo-ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metal-oxygen bond enthalpies in metal B-diketones are significantly larger than the metal-oxygen enthalpies of the corresponding metal oxides.

the metal-oxygen bond dissociation enthalpies of the complexes of β-dketoanates are significantly lower than the values reported previously for the metal alkoxides, which are the complexes of alcohols.
the enthalpy of gas-phase decomposition is a useful tool in the evaluation of the homolytic M-O bond-dissociations enthalpies of metal β-diketonates, which are difficult to obtain experimentally.
